abbreviations.HFmrEF: heart failure with mildly reduced ejection fraction
abbreviations.HFpEF: heart failure with preserved ejection fraction
abbreviations.HFrEF: heart failure with reduced ejection fraction

sections.title: Angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors
sections.text: There are no specific trials of ACE-I in patients with HFmrEF. The PEP-CHF trial was conducted in patients with HFpEF and included patients with an LVEF >40% but did not report outcomes according to LVEF. Many patients with HFmrEF will also have CAD, hypertension, or post-MI LV systolic dysfunction and therefore may already be treated with ACE-I. ACE-I use may be considered in patients with HFmrEF.

sections.title: Angiotensin receptor II type 1 receptor blockers
sections.text: There are no specific trials of ARBs in HFmrEF. The CHARM-Preserved trial missed its primary endpoint of CV death or HF hospitalizations. A retrospective analysis showed that candesartan reduced the number of patients hospitalized for HF among those with HFmrEF, and a recurrent-event analysis suggested a reduction in hospitalizations for HF in the broader CHARM-Preserved cohort. Many with HFmrEF may already be on an ARB for other CV indications; ARBs may be considered.

sections.title: Beta-blockers
sections.text: No specific trial of beta-blockade in HFmrEF. An IPD meta-analysis of landmark beta-blocker trials suggested similar reductions in CV and all-cause mortality (about 50%) for patients in sinus rhythm with HFrEF and HFmrEF. The SENIORS trial (nebi volol) reduced a composite primary endpoint in the overall population; no interaction between LVEF subgroup and nebivolol effect was observed. Many patients with HFmrEF may have another CV indication (e.g., AF or angina) for beta-blocker therapy; beta-blockers may be considered.

sections.title: Mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists
sections.text: No specific trial of MRAs in HFmrEF. Retrospective analysis of TOPCAT in patients with LVEF ≈45% found spironolactone reduced hospitalizations for HF in those with LVEF <55% with a similar trend for CV but not all-cause mortality. Treatment with an MRA may be considered in patients with HFmrEF.

sections.title: Angiotensin receptor–neprilysin inhibitor
sections.text: No specific trial of ARNI in HFmrEF. In PARAGON-HF (which included patients with EF ≈45%), the trial missed its primary endpoint overall, but a significant EF-by-treatment interaction was observed. Sacubitril/valsartan, compared with valsartan, reduced the likelihood of the primary composite outcome of CV death...

sections.title: General notes
sections.text: Across classes (ACE-I, ARB, beta-blockers, MRA, ARNI) there are limited or no trials specifically enrolling HFmrEF; many recommendations are extrapolated from trials in HFrEF or HFpEF or retrospective/subgroup analyses. Consideration of therapy often depends on comorbid CV indications (e.g., CAD, hypertension, prior MI, AF).
